architecture.title: NemoClaw on one Spark — the agent lives in a sandbox, the model stays on the host
architecture.caption: The nemoclaw CLI on the Spark creates an OpenShell sandbox and runs OpenClaw inside it. Every outbound connection from the sandbox goes through the OpenShell egress proxy, which allows only the hosts in the sandbox policy. Model calls go to inference.local, which OpenShell routes to local vLLM on the host's :8000. You reach the Web UI from your laptop through an ssh -L tunnel to 127.0.0.1:18789. Telegram is optional and uses long-polling, so no public URL is needed.

sequence.title: One agent turn — a tool call that the policy refuses
sequence.caption: The model asks for a tool; the agent runs it inside the sandbox; the egress proxy checks the policy and refuses a host that is not allowed with 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403'. The denial is logged (nemoclaw <name> logs, openshell term) and the agent reports the failure instead of leaking data. The tool name is illustrative; the 403 text is quoted from the playbook. This is the boundary lab 16-2 tests.

charts.title: Extra internet hosts each example agent needs (beyond inference.local)
charts.caption: From the NemoClaw applications playbook: the developer agent, deck reviewer and propose-only calendar agent run with no outbound network at all; the news digest adds its three example sources (news-sources preset) plus api.telegram.org for delivery. Fewer hosts, smaller blast radius.
